name: GitHub
description: The default home for Git repos, pull requests and code review.
use: Host your repo and review changes in pull requests.

name: GitLab
description: Git hosting with built-in CI, registry and issue tracking in one product.
use: Keep code, pipelines and issues in a single place.

name: Bitbucket
description: Atlassian's Git hosting, tightly linked with Jira.
use: Host code when your team already lives in Jira.

name: Gitea
description: Lightweight Git server you run yourself.
use: Self-host your repos on a small server.

name: Azure Repos
description: Git repos inside Microsoft's Azure DevOps suite.
use: Host code when your company is all-in on Azure DevOps.

name: GitHub Actions
description: CI/CD workflows defined in YAML, running right next to your GitHub repo.
use: Run tests on every pull request.

name: GitLab CI
description: GitLab's built-in pipelines, configured with .gitlab-ci.yml.
use: Build, test and deploy from the same GitLab project.

name: Jenkins
description: The veteran self-hosted automation server with a plugin for everything.
use: Run custom pipelines on your own build machines.

name: CircleCI
description: Hosted CI known for fast builds and good caching.
use: Speed up a large test suite with parallel jobs.

name: Buildkite
description: Hosted pipeline UI with agents running on your own machines.
use: Scale CI on your own hardware without running a CI server.

name: Azure Pipelines
description: Microsoft's CI/CD service, part of Azure DevOps.
use: Build .NET or any app inside Azure DevOps.

name: Docker
description: Packages your app and its dependencies into a container image using a Dockerfile.
use: Build one image that runs the same on your laptop and in production.

name: Cloud Native Buildpacks
description: Turns source code into a container image without writing a Dockerfile.
use: Get a secure, patched image by just pointing at your repo.

name: Nixpacks
description: Detects your language and builds an image automatically, using Nix under the hood.
use: Zero-config image builds for common app frameworks.

name: Podman
description: Daemonless, rootless alternative to Docker that reads the same Dockerfiles.
use: Build images without a root-level Docker daemon.

name: Kaniko
description: Builds container images inside a Kubernetes pod, no Docker daemon needed.
use: Build images in-cluster as part of a Kubernetes pipeline.

name: Terraform
description: Describe cloud resources in HCL and let Terraform create and update them.
use: Version-control your whole cloud setup.

name: OpenTofu
description: Open-source fork of Terraform, run by the Linux Foundation.
use: Terraform-style IaC under an open-source license.

name: Pulumi
description: Infrastructure as code written in TypeScript, Python, Go or C#.
use: Define cloud resources with loops and functions in a real language.

name: Ansible
description: Configures servers over SSH using YAML playbooks, no agent required.
use: Install packages and configure Nginx on a fleet of VMs.

name: AWS CloudFormation
description: AWS's native IaC service, using JSON or YAML templates.
use: Create AWS stacks with no extra tools.

name: AWS CDK
description: Write AWS infrastructure in TypeScript or Python; it compiles to CloudFormation.
use: Use real code and reusable constructs for AWS resources.

name: Vercel
description: Frontend and serverless platform made by the Next.js team. Push to Git, get a URL.
use: Host a Next.js app with preview deploys on every pull request.

name: Railway
description: Deploy apps and databases from a repo or image with almost no config.
use: Run an API plus Postgres without touching a server.

name: Fly.io
description: Runs your containers as fast micro-VMs close to your users worldwide.
use: Deploy a Docker app to several regions with one command.

name: Single VM + Nginx
description: One Linux server with Nginx in front of your app. The classic.
use: Run a small app cheaply when you are happy to manage the server.

name: Docker Compose on a VPS
description: A cheap VPS running your containers with docker compose up.
use: Run app, database and cache together on one $5 box.

name: AWS ECS (Fargate)
description: AWS's container service. Fargate runs containers without you managing servers.
use: Run containers on AWS without the complexity of Kubernetes.

name: Kubernetes (EKS/GKE/AKS)
description: The industry-standard container orchestrator, here as a managed cloud cluster.
use: Run many services with autoscaling, rollouts and self-healing.

name: Argo CD
description: Keeps your Kubernetes cluster in sync with what's in Git (GitOps).
use: Auto-deploy to Kubernetes when you merge to main.

name: Flux
description: CNCF GitOps toolkit that pulls changes from Git into your cluster.
use: Lightweight GitOps for Kubernetes without a UI.

name: Helm
description: The package manager for Kubernetes. Templates and versions your manifests.
use: Install and upgrade your app on Kubernetes as a versioned chart.

name: Spinnaker
description: Netflix's multi-cloud delivery platform with canary and blue/green rollouts.
use: Coordinate complex releases across many clouds and teams.

name: Built into platform
description: Let your hosting platform deploy on every push. Nothing extra to run.
use: Merge to main and the platform ships it.

name: Deploy script in CI
description: A CI job that SSHes into your server and restarts the app.
use: Simple push-to-deploy for a VM you manage yourself.

name: HashiCorp Vault
description: Full secrets platform: dynamic credentials, leasing, rotation and audit logs.
use: Issue short-lived database passwords to every service.

name: Doppler
description: Hosted secrets manager that syncs env vars to every environment and platform.
use: One place for secrets across dev, staging and production.

name: Infisical
description: Open-source secrets manager you can use hosted or run yourself.
use: Doppler-style secrets with the option to self-host.

name: AWS Secrets Manager
description: AWS's managed secrets store with automatic rotation for AWS databases.
use: Store and rotate RDS passwords for apps running on AWS.

name: SOPS
description: Encrypts secret files so they can be safely committed to Git.
use: Keep encrypted secrets next to your GitOps manifests.

name: Platform env vars
description: Environment variables set in your hosting platform's dashboard.
use: Add an API key in the dashboard and read it from process.env.

name: .env file
description: A plain-text file of KEY=value pairs sitting on the server.
use: Quick local development. Risky anywhere else.

name: Prometheus + Grafana
description: Open-source metrics collection plus dashboards. You run both.
use: Graph request rates and alert when error rates spike.

name: Grafana Cloud
description: Hosted Grafana, Prometheus and Loki with a generous free tier.
use: Metrics, logs and dashboards without running them yourself.

name: Datadog
description: All-in-one monitoring: metrics, logs, traces and APM in one SaaS.
use: See every service, host and trace in one place (and one big invoice).

name: New Relic
description: Full-stack observability platform with a free tier based on data volume.
use: APM and traces to find the slow endpoint.

name: Sentry
description: Catches errors and crashes with stack traces and the user context.
use: Get an alert with the exact line when production throws.

name: Uptime Kuma
description: Self-hosted uptime monitor with a status page.
use: Ping your site every minute and get a message when it's down.

name: Platform logs
description: The log viewer built into your hosting platform.
use: Tail logs in the dashboard when something looks off.
